title: First visit to an absorbing stop state
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $w$ be an input word, and let $	ext{stop}$ be a decidable predicate on its states. Suppose every configuration whose state satisfies $	ext{stop}$ is fixed by one step of $M$. If the run from a configuration $c$ reaches a configuration $d$ in a stop state at time $T$, then there is a time $t\le T$ at which the run equals $d$ and no stop state has been visited at any earlier time $j<t$.
hypotheses_covered: every configuration in a stop state is fixed by one step
configuration d has a stop state
run from c at time T equals d
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let a set of stop
control states be absorbing (a step from any configuration in a stop state changes
nothing), and suppose the run from a configuration $c$ reaches a configuration $d$ in a
stop state at time $T$. Then there is a time $t \le T$ such that no stop state is
visited strictly before $t$ and the run from $c$ at time $t$ equals $d$.
